[quote=the_crystalline_empire;61176422][b]Chapter I: Ivan[/b]
 
Ivan Ivanovic was a tragic figure, frequently lonely (even when others surrounded him) and frequently unparticipatory in the general affairs of those his age; he was severe and aloof to those who knew him, even to the point of publicly alienating himself for fear of being contaminated by some social contagion that would deign to destroy his view of the world. It was in this way that Ivans loneliness was inflicted upon himself, for he was so dull that not even his friend Jasper could stand to be with him more than an hour. The loneliness sometimes at night gnawed at the back of his mind, and he was frequently sorrowful, yet to him, this was the cost of a respectable life. 

One particular night, Ivan Ivanovic was making haste, in his usual black coat and grey cardigan,  to return to the Jasper E. Wiggins dorm hall, a ninety-year-old dorm hall with a ceiling that leaked blue fluid that Ivan swore was some form of anti-freeze when he made contact with a group of fellows (or he assumed they were fellows) dressed in costume

Giving pause to the group of fellows, he tilted his head ever so slightly and wondered to himself the absurdity of the matter, before shrugging it off as some odd frat event. 

Once the figures had passed, one of which had a tail to the costume, he made haste once more into the safe confines of his dorm hall, wherein he gave a warm greeting to his roommate, who was reading a My Little Pony comic, but of course he was, for Ivan never had normal roommates.

Know that my aunt kissed a cow once, stated the roommate, whose name was Leyoroy Jenkins.

Did the cow become a prince? Enquired Ivan, used to his roommates' non-sequitur comments.

I fear not, but she did get mad cow disease, replied Leyoroy calmly.

Speaking of mad cow disease, stated Ivan, I saw something strange on my way to the dorm, 

Yes? Enquired Leyoroy.

Yes, there were some costumed fellows; they were dressed like animals, replied Ivan.

Oh replied Leyoroy, Yes, I forgot to inform you,

Inform me of what? Enquired Ivan.

of the furries, replied Leyoroy, They make haste on this campus to make paths into unknown places, they appear and disappear, eluding those who persecute them, he continued, closing his comic.

Ivan frowned. He had heard of the idea of furry, strange people who liked to be animals or some other nonsense; however, a grim fascination came upon him, especially since they were seemingly so close. 

How might one find them? Ivan asked aloud, realising indeed he had asked the question that ought not to be asked.

Do I look like I know? Asked Leyoroy flippantly, I am merely the messenger, 

So are you a furry? Enquired Ivan, giving his roommate a side-eye and staring at the Twilight Sparkle plush that hung from the ceiling fan, the wings stretched out as if she were flying free, or at least desired to.

It isdebatableyou see there are some bronies who are also furriesand some furries who are broniesand some from both groups that disavow the other, replied Leyoroy.

Sounds complicated, replied Ivan.

It is, and it is a big point of contention at the National Convention for Animal Enthusiasts, replied Leyroy.

The NCAE? Ivan tilted his head, unsure about the matter of which he heard.

Yes, they meet every January, the Bronies and the Furries to debate and conclude the annual matters of the fandoms, stated Leyoroy.

Heck, sounds like the definition of social dissonance, stated Ivan.

Not so, for as you know, though I know you do not know, that the lord-emperor of the furries and the bronies, Augustus Sparkle Sunshine Smendelhammen IV, is the arbiter of unity, replied Leyoroy.

You now speak nonsense, replied Ivan with a laugh, I think you have drunk the coolant. 

I think not, retorted Leyoroy

I think yea, responded Ivan.

Ah, well, we ought to end this charade, replied Leyoroy with a wave of his hand, You will forget this quite soon, 

Ivan frowned and moved to his bed, hopping onto it (for he was short), though his mind was filled with questions, absurd as the matter was. 

Will you be retiring soon, my dear friend? enquired Leyoroy.

I shall, I am tired, replied Ivan.

Very well then, I shall pass on the light, replied Leyoroy

With that, Leyoroy moved off his bed and flicked off the lights, plunging the room into darkness.

It took Ivan but a moment to fall asleep, the roar of the window air conditioner placing him into the blissful embrace of his dreams.[/quote]

[b]Chapter 2: The summons[/b]

[spoiler]Indeed, by some unknown magic, Ivan casually forgot about the conversation that had taken place the night prior, as he arose from his bed and tiptoed around the room for fear of waking his roommate up.

You are awake, said a voice, startling him as he turned to face Leyoroy, who was indeed awake.

D-did I wake you? Asked Ivan in an apologetic tone.

Nah, replied Leyoroy, I was already awake.

Ivan breathed a sigh of relief as he turned once again to the sink and mirror that sat in the room.

I was thinking of our conversation last night, stated Leyoroy, mdoing some research, he continued, It seems that there is an active chapter of the NCAE here, he stated as if this was some light comment.

Ivan sighed as the memory of the last night walked into his head once more, Really? He stated, feigning interest between the bubbles of toothpaste.

Yeah, the club is called UWU, replied Leyoroy.

Isnt it actually OwO? Stated Ivan, finally doing away with the toothpaste.

Oh heavens no, replied Leyoroy, seeming slightly aghast at the mention of the word OwO, No, UWU is meant to be cute and funny, OwO is flirtatious in some manner, though of this I know not much about, he continued.

Huh, I did not know that, replied Ivan dryly, Anyways, you were saying about UWU?

Yes UWU, which stands for Understanding Wonderous Undertakings, replied Leyoroy.

And why does this matter? Asked Ivan, brushing his hair.

Because I emailed the president of the club last night after our conversation, and he is curious about you, stated Leyoroy

I am sorry, me? Replied Ivan, slightly confused, Why? How does he even know about me?!

Leyoroy laughed as he hopped off the bed, I told him about your sighting last night. 

So? Replied Ivan. Its a bit weird, he continued, moving to untie the bag that they had hung up to collect the blue ceiling drippings.

Anyways, they are meeting tonight, I think we should go, replied Leyoroy, ignoring Ivans seeming discomfort.

I have homework, replied Ivan bluntly, which was partially true, but it wasnt the type that wouldve taken all afternoon.

No, you dont, replied Leyoroy bluntly, seeing through his lie, So you will go? He stated.

Ivan sighed and replied, Only if you suffer with me also.

Leyoroy gave a big grin, Who says I will suffer? He laughed.

You are weird, beyond weird, replied Ivan, moving towards the door, I dont know how I stand you, he stated before opening it and leaving for the hallway, giving a hard stare at a disheveled figure who had just run down the hallway shouting something about weird figures in his mind.

 Ivan was not sure what to think about the events of the past two days, and the second day had yet to begin.[/spoiler]

[u]RR-1056 (Public Law 1090-56):[/u] Authorization of the Use of Military Force Against Threats to Elseyran Self-Determination and the Hochdeutsche Republics Vital National Security Interests in Kolionia

[i]Recognizing[/i] the importance of political self-determination in international law, norms and customs as well as the human rights of a people, 

[i]Alarmed[/i] by the undue and imperialistic influence of the government of Western View within the nation of Kolionia, 

[i]Establishing[/i] the foreign policy imperative of the Republic of the self-determination of Elseyran states from foreign influences, 

[i]Noting[/i] the need for prompt and decisive action to prevent a reprisal by the illegal occupation against independence,

[i]Having considered[/i] the Kolionian peoples call to action, 

The Republikenrat and the Hohenrat des Republik in the Republikenrat assembled do enact the following legislation for immediate implementation, 

SEC.101. The Republikenrat authorizes the Ministry of Defense and the Chancellor to utilize all necessary measures of military action to ensure the independence of the Kolionian state and that the national security interests of the Republic are protected for an indefinite time period, 

SEC.102. The Republic will implement a total embargo of Western View until such time that the illegal occupation of Kolionia ends, 

SEC.103. To further the diplomatic interests of the Republic and that of the Kolionian people the Republik will (a) consistently update the International Court of Justice on developing events in Kolionia as well as the actions of the Hochdeutsche Defense Forces (b) consistently maintain diplomatic lines with the government of Western View and representatives of the people of Kolionia, 

SEC.104. The Republic declares a total no-fly zone over Kolionian airspace to prevent further aggression by the illegal occupation, 

SEC.105. The Republic issues a notice to the international community(a) Notice to All Air Missions (NOTAM) is to be issued to warn all pilots in affected airspace of military operations, (b) Notice to Mariners (NOTMAR) is to be issued to warn all mariners in affected areas of military operations,
